title: Connecting your social channels: the big picture
summary: How WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Instagram, lead ads, Telegram and Google reviews reach your inbox, the two ways to connect them, and the order to do it in.

body.text: Once a channel is connected, its messages arrive in your **Social inbox** and you can reply from there. If you switch it on, the chatbot can also reply automatically. This guide shows what connects where; the guides after it go through each one step by step.
What you can connect

rows: Telegram chats, answered by the chatbot
Connected for the whole CRM by your CRM provider — see **Telegram**
New reviews, on their own inbox tab

body.text: Two ways to connect Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp

rows: Press **Connect Facebook** or **Connect WhatsApp**, sign in with Facebook and pick your Page or number.
Create an app on Meta's developer site and copy its details into the CRM.
A few minutes, no technical steps.
About an hour, following the guides step by step.
When your CRM provider has switched it on. If not, the card says it isn't set up yet.

body.text: Use the one-button connect if it's available — it's the quickest and nothing can be mistyped. See **Connect WhatsApp with one button**.
The order that saves time (own Meta app)

items: Set up your **Meta app** once. Messenger, Instagram, lead ads and WhatsApp all run through it — see **Step 1 — Create your Meta app**.
Connect the channels you want on top of it: **Messenger**, **Instagram**, **WhatsApp** and **lead ads**, each in its own guide.
Optionally add **Google reviews**.
Decide whether the **chatbot** should answer automatically. That's a separate switch on the Chatbot page — see **Turning the chatbot on and choosing where it runs**.

body.text: Connecting a channel only brings its messages into the inbox so you can answer them. Nothing is sent automatically unless you switch the chatbot on.
**Settings → Integrations** is for owners. Tokens and secrets you enter are stored encrypted and never shown again.

title: Step 1 — Create your Meta app (for Messenger, Instagram, lead ads and WhatsApp)
summary: Set up your own Meta app once, then copy its details into the CRM so Messenger, Instagram, lead ads and WhatsApp can reach your workspace.

body.text: If the **Connect Facebook** button on the **Meta (Messenger & Instagram)** card works for you, use that instead — it does all of this for you. This guide is for connecting **your own Meta app**.
1. On Meta's side: create the app

items: Go to **developers.facebook.com**, sign in, and create a new app of the **Business** type. Link it to your business portfolio.
Add the products you need: **Webhooks**, plus **Messenger**, **Instagram** and **WhatsApp** for the channels you'll use.

In **Business settings → Users → System users**, create a system user and generate a **permanent access token**. Give it the permissions your channels need: `pages_messaging`, `pages_manage_metadata` and `pages_read_engagement` (Messenger), `instagram_basic` and `instagram_manage_messages` (Instagram), `leads_retrieval` (lead ads), and `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management` (WhatsApp).
In the app's **App settings → Basic**, copy the **App secret**.

body.text: Use a **system user** token, not your personal one. Personal tokens expire after a while and the connection would quietly stop; a system user token doesn't expire.
2. In the CRM: save your app's details

items: Open **Settings → Integrations** and open the **Meta (Messenger & Instagram)** card.
In **Page access token (System User)**, paste the system user token and save.
In **Your Meta app's secret (own app only)**, paste the app secret and save. The CRM uses it to check that every message really came from your app.
In **Webhook verify token (own app only)**, type a password-like phrase of your own choosing — you'll enter the same phrase at Meta — and save.

body.text: 3. Point Meta at your workspace

The box **This workspace's own Meta app** on the same card shows your workspace's own **Callback URL** (and a **WhatsApp callback URL**). These addresses are unique to your workspace — copy them exactly.

items: In your Meta app, open **Webhooks**. Enter the **Callback URL** and the verify token you saved. Meta checks it straight away.
Subscribe **Instagram** to **messages** and **comments**, and your **Page** to **messages**, **feed** and **leadgen**.
Make sure your Facebook Page is subscribed to the app, so its events are delivered.
If the app also runs your WhatsApp number, set the **WhatsApp callback URL** under **WhatsApp → Configuration**, with the same verify token, and subscribe to **messages**.

body.text: The card shows **Connected** once the token is saved. Each channel then needs its own small steps — see the next guides.
If something goes wrong

items: **Meta won't verify the callback URL** — check the verify token at Meta is exactly the one you saved in the CRM, and that you copied the full callback address.
**Messages don't arrive** — check the app secret in the CRM matches the one in **App settings → Basic**. Messages signed with a different secret are refused.
**It worked, then stopped** — the token may have been a personal one that expired. Generate a system user token and save it again.

title: Connecting Facebook Messenger
summary: Get messages to your Facebook Page into the Social inbox.

body.text: The quick way

On **Settings → Integrations → Meta (Messenger & Instagram)**, press **Connect Facebook**, sign in with the Facebook account that manages your Page, and choose it under **Which Page does this workspace use?** Messages start arriving straight away.
With your own Meta app

items: Finish **Step 1 — Create your Meta app** first.
Make sure the **Page access token** you saved belongs to the Page whose messages you want.
Check your Page is subscribed to the app, with **messages** ticked.
Send your Page a message from another Facebook account. It should appear on the **Messenger** tab of the Social inbox within a few seconds.
Reply from the inbox to check replies reach Facebook too.

body.text: Until Meta approves your app's messaging permission (in Meta's App Review), only people with a role on your Meta app — admins, developers and testers — can message you through it. Everyone else's messages come through once it's approved.
To have the chatbot answer Messenger automatically, turn on **Messenger & Instagram DMs** on the Chatbot page. Connecting the channel alone doesn't send any automatic replies.
Disconnecting
If you used **Connect Facebook**, press **Disconnect** on the card. Messenger and Instagram messages, comments and lead ads from the Page stop arriving; conversations already in the CRM stay.

title: Connecting Instagram messages and comments
summary: Link your Instagram professional account to your Facebook Page so its direct messages and comments reach the inbox.

body.text: Instagram comes in through your Facebook Page, so connect Facebook first — with **Connect Facebook** or your own Meta app (see **Connecting Facebook Messenger**). Then:

items: Make your Instagram account a **professional** account (Business or Creator) if it isn't already.
Link it to your **Facebook Page** in the Page's settings, under linked accounts.
In the Instagram app, open **Settings → Messages and story replies → Connected tools** (Instagram sometimes moves this) and turn on **Allow access to messages**.

With your own Meta app: make sure the app has the **Instagram** product, the token has `instagram_basic` and `instagram_manage_messages`, and **Instagram** is subscribed to **messages** and **comments**.
Send your Instagram account a message from another account — it should appear on the **Instagram** tab of the inbox.

body.text: As with Messenger: until Meta approves your app's Instagram permissions, only people with a role on your Meta app (added as Instagram testers) can message you through it.

title: Connecting WhatsApp by entering your number's details
summary: Connect a WhatsApp Business number by copying its details from Meta into the CRM — the alternative to the one-button connect.

body.text: If the **WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)** card offers **Connect WhatsApp**, use that instead — see **Connect WhatsApp with one button**. This guide is for connecting the number through your own Meta app.
You need a business phone number that is **not** signed in to the ordinary WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app on a phone.
1. On Meta's side

items: Finish **Step 1 — Create your Meta app** first.
In your Meta app, add the **WhatsApp** product.
Under **WhatsApp → API Setup**, add your business number and copy its **Phone number ID**.
Make sure your system user token has `whatsapp_business_messaging` and `whatsapp_business_management`.

body.text: 2. In the CRM

items: Open **Settings → Integrations → WhatsApp Business (Cloud API)**.
Paste the **Phone number ID** and save.
Paste the token into **Access token (permanent, System User)** and save.

body.text: 3. Point WhatsApp at your workspace

items: Copy the **WhatsApp callback URL** from the box **This workspace's own Meta app** on the **Meta (Messenger & Instagram)** card.
In your Meta app under **WhatsApp → Configuration**, enter that address and the same verify token you saved on the Meta card, and subscribe to **messages**.
Message your business number from another phone — the chat should appear on the **WhatsApp** tab of the Social inbox.

body.text: The number must be used only for this. If it's still signed in to a WhatsApp app on a phone, Meta won't register it, or messages won't reach the CRM.
Only your own number's messages are accepted at your workspace's address — another business's can't land in your inbox.

title: Connecting Facebook & Instagram lead ads
summary: Have leads from your Facebook and Instagram lead forms created in the CRM automatically.

body.text: When someone fills in one of your Facebook or Instagram lead forms, the CRM creates a lead for them automatically — no downloading spreadsheets or typing them in.

items: Connect your Facebook Page first — with **Connect Facebook**, or your own Meta app (see **Step 1 — Create your Meta app**).
With your own Meta app: make sure the token has `leads_retrieval` (so the CRM can read the answers) and your **Page** is subscribed to **leadgen**.
Submit a test entry on one of your live forms and check a new lead appears in the CRM.

body.text: Each form entry is only ever turned into one lead, however many times Meta sends it. The ad and form it came from are saved with the lead, so you can see which campaign brought it in.
If a lead can't be read from Meta — usually because a permission is missing — it's recorded in **Settings → System Log** rather than lost. Check there if a test entry doesn't appear.

title: Connecting Google reviews
summary: Show new Google reviews of your business in the Social inbox, with an alert when one arrives.

body.text: New Google reviews appear on the **Google Reviews** tab of the Social inbox, with an alert, usually within about six hours of being posted.

items: In Google Cloud (console.cloud.google.com), create a key and switch on **Places API (New)** for it.
Find your business's **Place ID** with Google's Place ID finder — it starts with "ChIJ".
Open **Settings → Integrations → Google reviews**, paste the key into **Places API key** and the ID into **Place ID**, and save.

body.text: Both are needed before the card shows **Connected**. Reviews are shown as they are on Google; reply to them with **Reply on Google** in the inbox.
